issues.legal_issue: An acquiring authority or land acquisition officer cannot shift the date of the preliminary acquisition notification when determining compensation; only a constitutional court may do so in exceptional circumstances through its extraordinary jurisdiction.

A constitutional court may, under Article 142, shift the valuation date and direct compensation based on the market value prevailing on a later date when prolonged State inaction has deprived landowners of compensation and applying the original notification date would cause manifest injustice.

Landowners deprived of their property through acquisition are constitutionally entitled under Article 300-A to adequate compensation in accordance with law, and the State must ensure its prompt determination and payment.
